summary: All four ACs verified. .stale-banner uses position:sticky;top:0;z-index:200 with amber bg #fef3c7 / text #78350f / border #f59e0b. Dark mode override provides #451a03 bg and #fbbf24 text (8.97:1 contrast ratio, exceeds WCAG AA). No border-radius ensures edge-to-edge rendering. Banner colors are clearly distinct from .info-banner (blue), .error-banner (red), and .success-banner (green). No regressions: 1809/1809 tests pass.

comments.note: Both header and .stale-banner use position: sticky; top: 0. When the banner HTML is inserted before <header>, both will try to snap to top: 0 on scroll, causing them to visually overlap (banner wins via z-index: 200). This is a known CSS sticky sibling behaviour and is acceptable if intentional — the banner overlaps the header to remain prominent. Worth documenting the intended DOM placement when the HTML integration WP lands.
WCAG contrast ratios verified by calculation: light mode 8.15:1, dark mode 8.97:1 — both comfortably exceed WCAG AA (4.5:1). No accessibility issues.

summary: WP-002 CSS passes code review. .stale-banner rule is minimal, idiomatic, and correctly placed adjacent to .info-banner in styles.css.

Section comment follows the established /* --- ... --- */ pattern used throughout the file. Property ordering is conventional. Dark-mode override follows the [data-theme="dark"] block pattern used by all other banner variants.

z-index:200 over header z-index:100 is a deliberate and correct design decision for banner prominence. box-sizing:border-box is correctly included. Omission of display:flex is intentional — that belongs in the HTML integration WP.
WCAG contrast ratios verified by QA: 8.15:1 (light) and 8.97:1 (dark), both well above the 4.5:1 AA threshold. No blocking issues.

comments.note: The sticky sibling z-index design is correct and intentional: banner z-index:200 > header z-index:100. When the banner is inserted before <header>, both use position:sticky;top:0 — the banner "wins" the top slot during scroll because of higher z-index. This is the expected prominence behavior. The HTML-integration WP should document this as a placement constraint (banner must precede header in DOM order).
box-sizing: border-box is correctly included for predictable full-width padding behavior. No width: 100% is required since a block-level sticky element fills its containing block by default.

[documentation-forward] The .stale-banner CSS rule and its [data-theme="dark"] override should be documented in the GUI layer docs (or any relevant docs/agents/project-manifest section covering styles.css). Include: the intended DOM placement (before <header>), the z-index:200 sticky layering intent, the WCAG contrast ratios (light: 8.15:1, dark: 8.97:1), and the missing properties intentionally omitted (display:flex, align-items) that the HTML integration WP should add.
